result.text: Primary endpoint (mITT): event in 5/671 (0.7%) PAXLOVID vs 44/647 (6.8%) placebo; estimated difference in proportion -6.1% (95% CI: -8.2, -4.1; nominal p<0.0001). First key secondary endpoint (mITT1): event in 9/977 (0.9%) PAXLOVID vs 64/989 (6.5%) placebo; 5.6% absolute reduction (95% CI: -7.3% to -4.0%; p<0.0001), 86% relative reduction (95% CI: 72%, 93%).

key_safety.text: Favorable safety profile; most common adverse reactions were dysgeusia and diarrhea (in EPIC-HR PAXLOVID group 4.6% and 3.0% versus 0.1% and 1.5% placebo). Key safety concern is serious adverse reactions from drug-drug interactions.

citations.quote: adverse reactions associated with PAXLOVID use identified in clinical trials were dysgeusia and diarrhea, which were generally infrequent and mild in severity

The most common TEAEs (\ge 2\% incidence) in the EPIC-HR PAXLOVID group were dysgeusia and diarrhea, and these occurred at a higher frequency compared to the placebo group (4.6% and 3.0% versus 0.1% and 1.5%, respectively).
The key safety concern with PAXLOVID relates to the risk of serious adverse reaction

detail.text: Risk of serious adverse reactions due to drug interactions: PAXLOVID includes ritonavir, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, which may lead to greater exposure of certain concomitant medications, resulting in potentially severe, life-threatening, or fatal events.

citations.quote: PAXLOVID includes ritonavir, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, which may lead to greater exposure of certain concomitant medications, resulting in potentially severe, life-threatening, or fatal events. (4, 5.1, 7)

vote.text: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee met March 16, 2023; a majority (94%) of committee members agreed the overall benefit-risk assessment is favorable for PAXLOVID.

citations.quote: An Advisory Committee meeting was held on March 16, 2023 to discuss whether the available data support a favorable benefit-risk assessment

A majority (94%) of the committee members agreed that the overall benefit-risk assessment is favorable for PAXLOVID when used for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults who are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death.
